summary: Regional STS audience mismatch causing WIF->GCP service account mapping failures in dedicated-preview
description:
Issue summary: Over the last 24 hours, provisioning jobs that perform AWS->GCP workload identity federation (WIF) token exchange in dedicated-preview regions are failing to map the federated token to the intended GCP service account. Impact: A subset of dedicated-preview tenants experience failures during onboarding and CI tasks that need cross-cloud access; affected jobs see repeated 403/unauthenticated errors from GCP IAM when exchanging STS tokens. This blocks some Dedicated onboarding flows and debugging of private deployments.

Observed behaviour differs by region: us-east provisioning usually succeeds; eu-west and ap-south attempts fail consistently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger dedicated-preview provisioner to create tenant X in eu-west using aws-sts->gcp-wif exchange flow
2) Provisioner requests STS token from AWS (assume-role with session tags), then POSTs to GCP STS token exchange endpoint with audience parameter constructed from AWS account and role ARN
3) GCP responds with 401/403 and error 'Unable to map external identity to service account'

4) Retry attempts show same failure; manually performing the same exchange from an operator laptop (with identical payload) succeeds when targeted at us-east but fails when targeting eu-west endpoint.
logs: aws-sts response: AssumeRole success, SessionToken present, sessionDuration=3600

exchange POST to https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token:audience=//iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/pool/providers/provider - response 403 {"error":"requestForbidden","error_description":"External identity not mapped to any service account"}
provisioner logs: 'wif: audience string length 254 (truncated?)', 'retrying exchange (3/3)'
gcp audit: 'TokenExchangeFailed: aud mismatch: expected //iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/... provider/<provider-id> got //iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/... provider/<provider-id>-eu'
network: no abnormal packet loss between provisioner and GCP sts endpoints during time window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: audience string generation includes region suffix intermittently due to config merge; region suffix causes provider name mismatch in GCP WIF mapping.

Confirmed: dedicated-preview provisioning code concatenates region tag to provider id when region != us-east. This creates a provider identifier that does not exist in GCP IAM pool, leading to mapping failure.
Reproduction: built a minimal curl payload replacing audience with region-suffixed provider identifier reproduces 403 consistently against eu-west test pool.

Temporary mitigation: provisioning pipeline can be pointed to a manual provider alias by overriding audience construction in env var PROV_WIF_AUDIENCE_OVERRIDE. Applied for two affected tenants to unblock onboarding.
Risk assessment: change is scoped to dedicated-preview provisioning; unrelated production pools unaffected. However, several onboarding jobs and CI runs remain blocked until fix is deployed.
comments: Alyssa Chen (2026-03-10): Noticed spike in dedicated-preview failures after deploy of provisioning refactor earlier today. Opening ticket and rolling back candidate is not ideal due to unrelated fixes in that deploy.
Priya Nair (2026-03-10): Assigned. Adding SRE to triage and will add short-term override for affected customers. Linking to #support-private channel for customer comms.

Mateo Alvarez (SRE) (2026-03-11): Confirmed region suffix present in generated audience for eu-west. Verified provider with -eu suffix does not exist in project 123456. Proposed patch to audience formatter to strip region suffix for WIF provider ids.
Dev (2026-03-12): Created PR to fix audience generation: github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/1423. Adding automated unit test for provider id generation across regions.
Security (2026-03-12): Reviewed proposed change; no new privileges introduced. Confirmed that manual override should be logged and audited.
CS (2026-03-12): Notified affected tenant admins that onboarding would be retried; provided workaround to create manual provider alias if they prefer faster unblocking.
resolution: Workaround: provided PROV_WIF_AUDIENCE_OVERRIDE to unblock two tenants and documented steps. Permanent fix merged in PR #1423; rollout staged to dedicated-preview clusters (eu-west first) on 2026-03-13. Post-deploy verification shows successful STS exchanges and normal onboarding flows. Follow-up: add integration test across regions and add alert for audience mismatch errors (create metric 'wif.audience.mismatch').
notes_for_followup: 1) Add integration smoke tests that validate WIF audience construction for all supported regions
2) Instrument provisioner to emit structured audit log whenever audience is overridden
3) Run a scanning job to detect orphaned provider IDs in GCP projects (provider names with '-eu' suffix)
4) Add runbook entry in Confluence for temporary override procedure and customer communication template
